title: Enterprise RAG Vector Database & Hybrid Search Selection: pgvectorscale vs. Azure AI Search / OpenSearch vs. Milvus / Qdrant

tiers.tier: Tier 1: Unindexed / Naive Post-Filtered Vector DB (HNSW Top-K Then RBAC Filter)
tiers.architecture: Running standard HNSW vector search first (Top-50) and applying enterprise RBAC/tenant security filters in application code afterward

tiers.tier: Tier 2: Existing Relational DB Vector Extension (`PostgreSQL pgvector / pgvectorscale DiskANN`)
tiers.architecture: Storing vectors + relational metadata + transactional ACLs in existing PostgreSQL with StreamingDiskANN and BM25 (`pg_search`)

tiers.tier: Tier 3: Turnkey Cloud Enterprise Search PaaS (`Azure AI Search / AWS OpenSearch Serverless`)
tiers.architecture: Fully managed cloud hybrid search (BM25 + Vector + RRF + L2 Semantic Ranker) with native Entra ID / IAM document-level security trimming

tiers.tier: Tier 4: Dedicated Cloud-Native Vector Engine (`Milvus / Zilliz` or `Qdrant` Tiered RAM+NVMe + Pre-Filter Bitmap)
tiers.architecture: Purpose-built distributed vector engine with Roaring-Bitmap filtered HNSW/DiskANN traversal, sparse-dense hybrid RRF, partition keys, and NVMe/S3 tiering

scenarios.scenario: The 'Zero-Result Post-Filtering' Trap Under Selective Enterprise RBAC (`1%` Accessible Documents)
scenarios.question: A user with access to only 1% of a 50M-chunk SharePoint corpus searches for 'Q4 M&A target valuation'
scenarios.model_answer: Execute single-stage pre-filtered graph traversal (Roaring Bitmap ACL bitmask evaluated during HNSW/DiskANN hop expansion or Partition-Key isolation) -> returns 10 valid authorized chunks (98.4% Recall@10)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 1 fetches Global Top-50 vectors first and filters by ACL afterward -> all 50 hits belong to unauthorized departments, returning 0 results (38.5% recall)!

scenarios.scenario: Scale Inflection Point: `<10M` Chunks Departmental App vs. `200M+` Chunks Multi-Tenant Platform
scenarios.question: Architect must select a vector store for (A) a 4M-chunk internal CRM assistant already using PostgreSQL, and (B) a 250M-chunk global multi-tenant knowledge platform
scenarios.model_answer: Choose Tier 2 (`PostgreSQL + pgvectorscale DiskANN`) for Scenario A to avoid standing up a second database ($14K/mo, ACID joins); choose Tier 3 (`Azure AI Search`) or Tier 4 (`Milvus/Qdrant` with NVMe DiskANN tiering) for Scenario B ($22K–$31K/mo)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Deploying a 12-node distributed Milvus cluster for a 2M-chunk app wastes $40K/yr in ops; conversely, forcing 250M 1536-d vectors into unsharded Postgres RAM HNSW triggers vacuum stalls.

scenarios.scenario: Exact SKU / Error-Code / Clause Lookup (`ERR-4092-BX` or `ISO-27001 A.8.2`) Where Dense Vectors Fail
scenarios.question: Engineer queries 'Fix for error code ERR-4092-BX on firmware v4.12'
scenarios.model_answer: Run parallel Dense Vector + Sparse BM25/SPLADE retrieval fused via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF, k=60) + Cross-Encoder Semantic Reranker (97.4%–97.8% exact-match hit rate)
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Dense-only vector search dilutes exact alphanumeric codes into generic 'firmware error' neighbors, missing the exact bulletin (44.0% hit rate).

scenarios.scenario: Preventing 100% RAM HNSW Explosion on 100M+ Vectors via Binary/Scalar Quantization & NVMe DiskANN
scenarios.question: Host 100M 1536-dimensional float32 vectors without paying $54,000/month for 1.2 TB of pure cloud DRAM
scenarios.model_answer: Enable Scalar Quantization (`SQ8`) / Binary Quantization (`BQ` with 4x oversampling rescore) or NVMe `DiskANN` in Qdrant / Milvus / Azure AI Search -> cuts RAM footprint by 75%–92% while preserving >98% recall
scenarios.tier1_3_failure: Tier 1 stores uncompressed FP32 HNSW graphs entirely in memory, wasting 54.0% of cluster budget on oversized RAM instances.

perturbation_checks.check: High-Cardinality Multi-Tenant Isolation (25,000 Enterprise Customer Tenants in One Index)
perturbation_checks.perturbed: 18.0 ms P99 Latency | 98.2% Filtered Recall (Tenant Partition-Key Sub-Indexing Avoids 25,000 Separate Collections)

perturbation_checks.check: High-Frequency Document Permission Revocation (ACL Group Membership Change)
perturbation_checks.perturbed: 0.0% Leak (Security-Group OID Filter Evaluated at Query Time Without Re-Embedding Chunks)

key_findings: For `<10M` vectors where the enterprise already runs PostgreSQL, Tier 2 (`PostgreSQL + pgvectorscale DiskANN + pg_search BM25`) delivers 91.5% filtered recall at the lowest total TCO ($14K/mo) with zero new infrastructure silos.

For `10M–100M` enterprise knowledge bases requiring turnkey Microsoft 365 / Entra ID security trimming, hybrid BM25+vector RRF, and L2 semantic reranking with zero K8s ops, Tier 3 (`Azure AI Search / Managed OpenSearch`) achieves 96.8% recall and 97.4% exact-SKU accuracy.

For `100M–1B+` high-QPS multi-tenant platforms, Tier 4 (`Milvus / Zilliz` or `Qdrant` with Roaring-Bitmap pre-filtered HNSW, partition keys, and NVMe/SQ8 quantization) delivers 98.4% filtered recall at 16.5 ms P99 latency while cutting RAM TCO by 67.6% vs. unquantized clusters.
